title: Micro-OKR Habit Compressor — 14d focus log
content:
Purpose:
Short, messy scratchpad for a 14-day micro-OKR + habit experiment. Trying to compress attention into a tiny set of measurable behaviors and one throughput metric so I can ship more predictable output without burning cycles on overthinking.

Why this form factor:
- Long-term OKRs are good but feel diffuse; a 14d horizon forces tighter hypotheses.
- Habit compression: reduce the number of daily decisions so the signal (work shipped) dominates noise (context switching).
- Want a single northstar metric for the window + 2 supporting behavior KPIs.

Hypothesis (H0):
If I commit to 3 concrete micro-actions each day and protect a 90-minute deep block, I will increase weekly shipped outcomes by 40% over baseline (baseline = average of last 3 weeks).

Primary metric (northstar):
- "deliverable-throughput": number of small deliverables completed per week (deliverable = merged PR, shipped doc, or deployed tiny feature). Goal = 6 in the 14-day window (approx 3/week). Baseline ~ 2.

Supporting behavior KPIs:
1) Deep block integrity: % of scheduled deep blocks completed (goal 75%+).
2) Micro-action adherence: count of days I complete 3+ micro-actions (goal = 10/14).

Micro-actions (concrete):
- Action A: Draft 1 PR description + checklist before coding (reduces rework).
- Action B: 25-min focused design/outline for next deliverable (pomodoro).
- Action C: 15-min pairing or sync to unblock unique dependency.

Cadence and rituals:
- Morning: 10-min planning, select 1 deliverable and set micro-actions.
- Midday: 90-min protected deep block (no meetings, no Slack).
- EOD: 10-min async writeup: what shipped, blockers, next-day focus.
- Twice-weekly short retro (15m) to capture patterns and failure modes.

Signals to watch (leading/lagging):
- Leading: number of micro-actions completed, deep block starts vs. scheduled, interruptions count.
- Lagging: merged PRs, docs published, unresolved follow-ups.

Failure modes (and fallback):
- FM1: Meetings encroach on deep blocks. Mitigation: switch one deep block to early morning and mark as "no-core" on calendar; escalate recurring conflict to manager.
- FM2: Micro-actions feel busywork and don't convert to deliverables. Mitigation: require one micro-action to be explicitly tied to next deliverable's acceptance criteria.
- FM3: Over-optimistic goal setting -> demotivation. Mitigation: mid-window recalibration; if week 1 throughput << baseline, downscale goals and treat as learning iteration.

Data capture (manual lightweight):
- Daily TODO line: deliverable + micro-actions ticked (example: "DOC-logging: PR desc ✓, outline ✓, sync ✗").
- End-of-week tally: update northstar and behavior KPIs in a single line.

Template (one-line entries):
[YYYY-MM-DD] Deliverable: <short desc> | Actions: A,B,C ticks | DeepBlock: 90/60/0min | Notes: blockers

Example entries (realistic):
[2026-02-14] Deliverable: perf-doc-embed-routing | Actions: A✓,B✓,C✓ | DeepBlock: 90 | Notes: removed stale cache experiment, ready for review
[2026-02-15] Deliverable: pr-123-optimize-kv-cache | Actions: A✓,B✗,C✗ | DeepBlock: 60 | Notes: unexpected infra work, paired with infra-eng

Weekly retro prompts (15m):
- What shipped vs planned?
- Which micro-action most correlated with progress?
- Biggest interruption pattern?
- One small experiment for next week to increase signal/noise.

Mini experiments to try this window:
- E1: Two-day early-morning deep-block instead of afternoon (test for fewer interruptions).
- E2: Swap one micro-action to writing acceptance tests first; measure rework.
- E3: Block Slack except for DMs during deep blocks; measure perceived focus and actual throughput.

Acceptance for "deliverable":
- PR can be merged without major rework OR doc accepted by 1 peer OR small feature toggled to prod behind flag.

Stakes and tradeoffs:
- Trade memory of long-term projects for short-term throughput. That is intentional for the experiment window.
- If a downstream team is affected, flag and revert to safer cadence.

Open questions (to answer during window):
- Q1: Is 90 minutes the right minimum or should I aim for two 60-min blocks?
- Q2: Does combining pair-sync with a deep block help or fragment attention?
- Q3: Can one micro-action be automated (PR template) to save decision cost?

Attachments I should create by EOW:
- One-line weekly scoreboard (spreadsheet row)
- Short checklist template (PR desc template)
- 2 mini-retro notes with examples of interruptions

Slack/Links to reference: 
- Slack thread with team about blocking policy: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234567/p1678901234567
- Linear ticket for this experiment: https://linear.app/REDWOOD/issue/PRJ-721-micro-okr

Final quick blueprint for day-1:
- Pick one deliverable and write acceptance criteria (20m).
- Set calendar block for 90m earliest available.
- Draft PR description + checklist before starting code.
- Do one 15-min unblock sync if needed.
- Log the day using template line.

Notes-to-self: keep entries short. This is an experiment, not a lifestyle commitment. If it improves throughput and morale, consider 4-week run next quarter and iterate on metrics.

-- end of scratchpad --
